# 2 Samuel Chapter 13 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 182r–183r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_013_page_001.jpg, 2SA_013_page_002.jpg, 2SA_013_page_003.jpg

---

**1** Now after this, Absalom the son of David had a beautiful sister whose name was Tamar, and Amnon the son of David loved her.

**2** And Amnon was so tormented that he made himself ill on account of Tamar his sister, for she was a virgin, and it seemed impossible in Amnon's eyes to do anything to her.

**3** Now Amnon had a friend whose name was Jonadab the son of Shimeah, David's brother, and Jonadab was a very shrewd man.

**4** And he said to him, "Why are you so haggard, O son of the king, morning after morning? Will you not tell me?" And Amnon said to him, "I love Tamar, the sister of my brother Absalom."

**5** And Jonadab said to him, "Lie down on your bed and pretend to be ill. When your father comes to see you, say to him, 'Please let my sister Tamar come and give me food to eat, and let her prepare the food in my sight, that I may see it and eat from her hand.'"

**6** So Amnon lay down and pretended to be ill. When the king came to see him, Amnon said to the king, "Please let my sister Tamar come and make a couple of heart-shaped cakes in my sight, that I may eat the food of the sick from her hand."

**7** Then David sent word to Tamar at the palace, saying, "Go now to the house of your brother Amnon and prepare food for him."

**8** So Tamar went to the house of her brother Amnon, where he was lying down. She took dough and kneaded it and made cakes in his sight and baked them.

**9** Then she took the pan and set them before him, but he refused to eat. And Amnon said, "Send everyone out from me." So everyone went out from him.

**10** Then Amnon said to Tamar, "Bring the food into the inner chamber, that I may eat from your hand." So Tamar took the cakes she had made and brought them to her brother Amnon in the inner chamber.

**11** And when she brought them near to him to eat, he seized her and said to her, "Come, lie with me, my sister."

**12** She said to him, "No, my brother, do not force me, for such a thing is not done in Israel. Do not do this disgraceful thing.

**13** As for me, where could I carry my shame? And as for you, you would be as one of the fools in Israel. Now therefore, please speak to the king, for he will not withhold me from you."

**14** But he would not listen to her voice. He was stronger than she, and he forced her and lay with her.

**15** Then Amnon hated her with a very great hatred, for the hatred with which he hated her was greater than the love with which he had loved her. And Amnon said to her, "Get up! Go!"

**16** She said to him, "No — for this wrong in sending me away is greater than the other that you did to me." But he would not listen to her.

**17** He called his servant who attended him and said, "Put this woman out of my presence and bolt the door after her."

**18** Now she was wearing a robe of long sleeves, for thus were the virgin daughters of the king dressed in robes. So his servant put her out and bolted the door after her.

**19** And Tamar put ashes on her head and tore the robe of long sleeves that was on her. She put her hand on her head and went away, crying aloud as she went.

**20** And her brother Absalom said to her, "Has Amnon your brother been with you? Now be silent, my sister — he is your brother. Do not take this thing to heart." So Tamar remained, desolate, in the house of her brother Absalom.

**21** When King David heard all these things, he was very angry.

**22** But Absalom spoke to Amnon neither good nor bad, for Absalom hated Amnon because he had forced his sister Tamar.

**23** After two full years, Absalom had sheepshearers at Baal-hazor, which is near Ephraim, and Absalom invited all the sons of the king.

**24** And Absalom came to the king and said, "Behold, your servant has sheepshearers. Please let the king and his servants go with your servant."

**25** But the king said to Absalom, "No, my son, let us not all go, lest we be a burden to you." He pressed him, but he would not go, yet he gave him his blessing.

**26** Then Absalom said, "If not, please let my brother Amnon go with us." And the king said to him, "Why should he go with you?"

**27** But Absalom pressed him until he sent Amnon and all the sons of the king with him.

**28** Then Absalom commanded his servants, saying, "Watch now — when Amnon's heart is merry with wine, and I say to you, 'Strike Amnon!' — then kill him. Do not fear. Have I not commanded you? Be strong and be men of valor."

**29** So the servants of Absalom did to Amnon as Absalom had commanded. Then all the sons of the king rose, and each mounted his mule and fled.

**30** While they were on the way, the report came to David: "Absalom has struck down all the sons of the king, and not one of them is left."

**31** Then the king rose and tore his garments and lay on the ground, and all his servants stood by with their garments torn.

**32** But Jonadab the son of Shimeah, David's brother, spoke and said, "Let not my lord suppose that they have killed all the young men, the sons of the king, for Amnon alone is dead. For by the command of Absalom this has been determined from the day that he forced his sister Tamar.

**33** Now therefore, let not my lord the king take it to heart, thinking all the sons of the king are dead, for Amnon alone is dead."

**34** Meanwhile Absalom fled. And the young man who kept watch lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, many people were coming along the road behind him from the side of the mountain.

**35** And Jonadab said to the king, "Behold, the sons of the king have come; as your servant said, so it has come to pass."

**36** And as soon as he had finished speaking, behold, the sons of the king came and lifted up their voices and wept. And the king also and all his servants wept very bitterly.

**37** But Absalom fled and went to Talmai the son of Ammihud, king of Geshur. And David mourned for his son day after day.

**38** So Absalom fled and went to Geshur and remained there three years.

**39** And the spirit of King David longed to go out to Absalom, for he was comforted concerning Amnon, since he was dead.

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

**Verse 2 — "tormented... made himself ill":** The Hebrew *vayetser* (was distressed/narrow) combined with *lehitchalot* (to make oneself sick) portrays Amnon's obsession as a physical affliction. The combination of psychological anguish and self-induced illness is deliberate — this is desire experienced as disease.

**Verse 3 — "shrewd":** The Hebrew *chakham* means "wise," but Jonadab's "wisdom" is employed for evil purposes. I render "shrewd" to distinguish this calculating cunning from the true wisdom celebrated in Proverbs and elsewhere.

**Verse 12 — "disgraceful thing":** The Hebrew *nevalah* is one of the strongest moral condemnations in the Hebrew Bible, used for acts that violate the fundamental order of Israelite society. Tamar's speech is legally precise and rhetorically powerful — she names the act before it occurs.

**Verse 15 — the reversal:** The narrator's observation is one of the most psychologically acute statements in ancient literature. The cognate accusative construction (*the hatred which he hated her... the love which he had loved her*) creates a formal parallelism that exposes the structural identity of obsession and revulsion.

**Verse 18 — "robe of long sleeves":** The Hebrew *ketonet passim* is the same term used for Joseph's garment (Gen 37:3). This verbal link invites the reader to see Tamar's story as a recurrence of sibling violence within the covenant family. The garment, a mark of royal virginity, is torn — the status it represented has been destroyed.

**Verse 21 — David's anger and inaction:** The MT records only David's anger. The LXX adds that David did not punish Amnon because he loved him as his firstborn. This addition, likely original (supported by 4QSamᵃ), explains the gap between David's emotion and his failure to act — a pattern that will cost him dearly.

**Verse 22 — "neither good nor bad":** This phrase indicates complete silence — Absalom did not engage Amnon at all. The narrator signals that this silence is not forgiveness but calculation. The hatred is named explicitly: it is *on account of* the forcing of Tamar.

**Consistent terms:** Absalom (Avshalom), the LORD (YHWH), virgin (betulah), disgraceful thing (nevalah).

*— LOGOS*
